verdict.rationale: cubic documents custom agents as review rules that enforce an organization's best practices across pull requests. They are defined in cubic.yaml or adopted from a community library, and cubic automatically reviews new PRs. An independent commenter confirms the rules are plain-English text kept in the codebase. What is not shown is whether these agents act as gating pre-merge checks rather than review comments, or whether checks like 'docs updated' or 'tests cover new paths' are supported. missing for 10: first-party docs showing custom agents written in plain natural language, documented pass/fail or merge-blocking status-check behavior, examples of docs-updated or test-coverage checks, hands-on corroboration of reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I define custom agentic pre-merge checks in plain language — 'docs updated', 'tests cover new paths' — that run on every PR

citations.quote: Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
You can also adopt existing agents from the community library with a single click.
